{"findings":[{"rule_id":"MF-005","evidence":[{"kind":"title_block","ref":"heat_treatment","page":1,"quote":"---"}],"comment":"The title block heat treatment field is '---' while note N3 on page 1 specifies case hardening to 55~60 HRC with a case depth of 0.8~1.2 mm and that threads are to be kept soft. The title block must reflect the required heat treatment so it is not missed during manufacturing planning; update the heat_treatment field to reference the case hardening requirement or point to note N3.","recommended_correction":"Change the title block heat_treatment field from '---' to a value consistent with note N3, such as 'CASE HARDENED' or 'SEE NOTE N3'."},{"rule_id":"WPS-004","evidence":[{"kind":"note","ref":"N5","page":1,"quote":"# FINISH: I.Z.B.P. (TRIVALENT)"},{"kind":"dimension","ref":"D11","page":1,"quote":"20"},{"kind":"note","ref":"N3","page":1,"quote":"1) TO BE CASE HARDENED UPTO 55~60 HRC.
2) CASE DEPTH 0.8~1.2mm.
3) THREADS TO BE KEEP SOFT.
4) RETAPPING TO BE DONE AFTER SURFACE TREATMENT AT SUPPLIER END.( IF APPLICABLE )"}],"comment":"Note N5 calls for zinc plating (I.Z.B.P.) but dimension D11 defines the M16 thread length without any allowance for plating thickness, which will cause the plated threads to be oversize and fail to mate. Although note N3 mentions retapping after surface treatment, the drawing must explicitly state that thread dimensions allow for plating buildup or define pre-plate thread limits so the machinist knows what to cut before plating.","recommended_correction":"Add a note or modify the thread callout to specify that thread dimensions are pre-plate and must allow for the I.Z.B.P. plating thickness, or provide explicit pre-plate thread tolerances."}]}
